1.x: **Founded:** **1867, Bombay**, by **Dr. Atmaram Pandurang**, helped by **Keshab Chandra Sen** (visits 1864, 1867); grew out of the **Paramahansa Sabha**; Maharashtra-based; the Brahmo Samaj influenced it.

**Leaders:** **M.G. Ranade** (joined 1870, **chief mentor** – gave it an all-India character), **R.G. Bhandarkar** (Sanskrit scholar and orientalist; first Indian V-C of Bombay University), **N.G. Chandavarkar**.

**Beliefs:** **monotheism**, attached to the Maharashtra **bhakti** tradition; aimed to **reform Hindu society from within**; relied on education and **persuasion**, not confrontation; did not outright forbid image worship.

**Four-point agenda:** (i) disapproval of **caste**, (ii) **women's education**, (iii) **widow remarriage**, (iv) **raising the age of marriage** for both sexes; the abolition of untouchability was outside the list.
Ranade and the Indian National Social Conference

**Indian (National) Social Conference:** founded by **M.G. Ranade** and **Raghunath Rao**; first session **Madras, 1887**; met **at the same time and venue as the INC** – its "social reform cell", because the Congress (Dadabhai, 1886) kept to political questions only.
**Ranade** relied on **legislation**; worked against child marriage and purdah; also the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870).

r: Social, religious, political and economic reforms are interdependent and must proceed together

1.x: Prarthana Samaj = Atmaram Pandurang 1867; chief mentor Ranade; agenda = caste, women's education, widow remarriage, marriage age.

2.x: **Founded:** **1849, Maharashtra (Bombay)**, by **Dadoba Pandurang**, **Durgaram Mehtaji** (of the Manav Dharma Sabha, Surat) and others; Bipan Chandra dates religious reform in Bombay from **1840** by the Mandali.
**First socio-religious organisation in Maharashtra** – religious reform in Bombay began with it, before the Prarthana Samaj (1867).
**A secret society**; believed in **one God**; aim: **against idolatry and the caste system** – members **ate food cooked by lower castes**; backed **widow remarriage and women's education**.
**Branches:** **Poona**, Satara; exposure in 1860 ended it; reorganised as the Prarthana Samaj (1867).
**Manav Dharma Sabha:** founded at **Surat, 1844**, by **Durgaram Manchharam (Mehtaji)** with Dadoba Pandurang – forerunner of the Paramahansa Mandali.
Paramahansa Mandali = secret, 1849, Dadoba Pandurang, anti-caste and anti-idolatry.

3.x: **Leader:** **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio** (1809-31), Anglo-Indian teacher at **Hindu College** (1826-31); inspired by the **French Revolution**; first nationalist poet of modern India.
**Derozians:** radical rationalism – question all authority; women's rights; demanded press freedom, trial by jury, Indians in higher services.
**Academic Association (1828):** debating forum of Derozio and his students.
**Dismissed** from Hindu College in **1831**; died of cholera the same year. **Failure:** radicalism bookish, no link with the masses.
Young Bengal = Derozio, Hindu College, Academic Association 1828, removed 1831.
